title: Make the commands work on a default Windows box, and stop headers hiding a testable gate

history.detail:
CONDITIONAL: CONDITIONAL — round 1. Audited 5f2b290 (with b0b9679, e33ec1e, 5cc1906), main checkout. Sprint file read fresh — it WAS amended mid-build (Req 5 became the version-marker requirement, the old Req 5 moved to Req 6, and Req 2 gained the clearable path I flagged last turn). Audited against the current file and the current numbering.

Neither FAIL trigger fired. Reqs 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and the first half of Req 1 are met. One requirement is not, and the reason it is not is the reason its criterion was written the way it was.

================================================================
ANSWERING YOUR QUESTION FIRST — THE REQ 3 SIMULATION MEETS THE BAR
================================================================

You asked whether the alias-toggle simulation counts or whether a from-scratch python.org install is still needed. It counts, and the criterion is the reason: "confirm this was attempted and that the outcome — established or not obtainable — is recorded plainly. **An inference from the macOS proof is a FAIL.**" The FAIL trigger is inference from macOS. You did not infer; you ran it on the real VM, produced the shape that matters (python3 unrecognized, python a real 3.13.14), exercised both a read command and a write command through the resolved interpreter, and labelled it a simulation rather than a from-scratch install. That is the outcome recorded plainly.

One thing that strengthens it further, and is worth putting on the record rather than leaving as a caveat: the untested `py` branch is unreachable in the scenario the requirement names. findPython3Interpreter resolves python3 -> python -> py in order, so `py` is only ever consulted when `python` is absent or is not Python 3. A python.org install creates both `python` and `py`, so on the very machine the requirement describes, resolution stops at `python` and `py` is never reached. "py stays untested" is therefore not a gap in the proof — it is a branch the requirement's own scenario cannot enter. Say that in the notes rather than carrying it as an open caveat; it reads as a weakness right now and it is not one.

================================================================
REQ 2 — MET, AND THE UNTESTED HALF IS COVERED BY CONSTRUCTION
================================================================

You flagged that the Python-prerequisite warning specifically was not re-triggered live. It does not need to be, and I verified why rather than accepting the reasoning:
  - Non-ASCII in non-comment code in install.js: ZERO. Checked by parsing the file and stripping
    comment text, not by grepping the whole file (which still shows 79 comment lines, all prose).
  - Real captured stdout, run twice against a scratch target — a clean install, then a run with a
    genuine CLAUDE.md conflict: 1896 and 2764 characters, ZERO non-ASCII in either. The conflict
    section is present in the second.
If the source can emit no non-ASCII byte, and ASCII is confirmed to render correctly on that console, then every message it prints is covered — including the one not separately triggered. Static plus dynamic together establish it; neither alone would. That is the right pair of tests and it is why the gap you flagged honestly is not actually a gap.

The live Windows half is the part that could not be substituted, and you did it: a genuine conflict triggered on the real VM, raw PowerShell output read, every dash a plain character. Not derived from code-page reasoning.

================================================================
REQ 1, FIRST HALF — MET
================================================================

Grepped all twelve command files rather than the three named, as the criterion instructs: zero hardcoded `/tmp` paths anywhere. The three outstanding files follow sprint 12's shipped working-directory-relative pattern rather than a second invented one. resolve_text() fails via die() naming the attempted path instead of raising.

================================================================
FINDING 1 (blocking) — REQ 1's SECOND HALF WAS REASONED, NOT RUN
================================================================

The criterion: "confirm `sprint-new.md` no longer depends on the Write tool, and that a headless Master Controller **can actually create a sprint** under the scoped profile. **If that was reasoned rather than run, it is not met** — it is the exact inference sprint 12 disproved."

There is no record of that run. I looked in the commit messages for 5cc1906..HEAD, in sprint 14's own state-file history (one event: sprint_started), and in the permission-scope findings document. Nothing. Your handoff does not claim one either — it claims the file gained the fallback, which is the change, not the demonstration.

This one is not a formality. The criterion demanded a run specifically because the analogous inference was wrong once already, and it turns out to be wrong again here — see Finding 2, which is what a run would have surfaced immediately.

================================================================
FINDING 2 (blocking) — THE NEW NOTE STATES SOMETHING THAT IS NOT TRUE
================================================================

sprint-new.md's new headless note says:

  "if the Write tool is unavailable (a headless Master Controller session under a scoped permission
   profile **never has it** — this was the second defect here: the instruction above required Write,
   and nothing else was offered, so headless Master Controller could not create a sprint at all)"

A headless Master Controller has the Write tool. Read the shipped profiles in run-role.js:
    master-controller   disallowedTools: []
    dev-team-1          disallowedTools: []
    qa1                 disallowedTools: ['Edit', 'Write']
    liveqa              disallowedTools: ['Edit', 'Write']
Only qa1 and liveqa have it removed. That is sprint 12's own deliberate design — those two roles never write source; Master Controller does, because writing sprint files is its job.

And sprint 12's findings document already recorded this by running it: "The `Write` tool, writing a file WITHIN the working directory, succeeded under plain `acceptEdits` alone — CONFIRMED, no allowlist needed." That was Master Controller's own scenario, tested directly.

So the parenthetical describes a defect that did not exist for this role. What sprint 12 actually found for Master Controller was different and narrower: `node scripts/run-lifecycle.js new` needed an explicit allowlist entry, which it has.

WHY THIS MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING A WORDING NIT: the note tells a headless Master Controller that it "never has" a tool it does have. A role reading its own command file and believing that will route around a working path — and the printf fallback, while harmless in itself, is now presented as a necessity rather than a belt-and-braces alternative. This is the fourth time in four sprints that a claim in shipped guidance has not survived checking (sprint 12's heredoc, sprint 12's /tmp destination, sprint 13's "docs/sprints never ships," this), and every one of them was a claim that a run would have settled.

REQUIRED FIX, both findings together, because they are one root cause:
  1. Run it. Launch a headless Master Controller under the scoped profile and have it create a sprint.
     That is the criterion, and it settles Finding 2 as a side effect.
  2. Correct the note to what the run establishes. If Write works for this role — and both the shipped
     profile and sprint 12's confirmed finding say it does — then the printf form is a portable
     alternative worth documenting, not a workaround for a missing tool. Keep it; describe it
     accurately.

================================================================
REQS 4, 5, 6, 7 — MET
================================================================

Req 4 — read cold against sprint 10's header, which I pulled from 3-done to compare rather than trusting the quotation. The new bullet quotes it verbatim, names the actual defect precisely (the pairing of a stated impossibility with a "record nothing" off-ramp offered in the same breath, before anyone has tried), and tells Master Controller what to write instead. Sprint 10's header fails under it unambiguously. The rule is written correctly.

Req 5 — the invariant is stated at writeInstalledVersion()'s write site and matches what the code does. It is careful in exactly the place the criterion warns about: it states what the guarantee covers (FRAMEWORK_OWNED, including scripts/launcher), what it does not (USER_OWNED tracked files, which syncTrackedUserOwnedFile can deliberately leave un-synced on an unresolved conflict without aborting), and that the read side degrades the opposite way on purpose. It also names the node_modules case, which nobody asked for and which is the one a consumer would actually get wrong. It does not promise more than the code delivers.

Req 6 — package.json 0.1.15.

Req 7 — ran everything: ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED; ALL LAUNCHER TESTS PASSED, 125 OK (up 2, matching the two new Req 2 tests); verify-tarball.sh TARBALL VERIFICATION PASSED, "Installed 0.1.15 (first install)".

The two new launcher tests are the right pair — a static scan for non-ASCII outside comments, and a dynamic check on real captured stdout with both a conflict and a missing-interpreter warning firing. I reproduced both independently and both hold.

================================================================
INFORMATIONAL
================================================================

1. The baseline-fixture breakage is on its fourth occurrence, root cause still unfixed. I see sprint 16 is now drafted for it ("make the baseline table maintain itself and stop tests breaking on its drift"), which is the right outcome — recording that it took four occurrences, and that I first flagged the generator drifting in sprint 9's notes, so the interval is on the record rather than in a handoff.
2. docs/sprints/registry.json is modified and uncommitted, and sprints 15 and 16 are untracked in 1-todo. Not in this diff; flagging for whoever commits next.

RECOMMENDATION

One run and one correction. The run is the requirement; the correction falls out of it. Then round 2 is short — everything else is verified and I have no other open items.

Worth saying plainly: this sprint's own Req 4 is a rule about not asserting what you have not attempted, and the one thing holding it up is an assertion that was not attempted. That is not irony worth a joke, it is the reason the rule is being written.

PASS: PASS — round 2. Audited 813316b with bookkeeping edfdcff, main checkout. Sprint file re-read fresh; `git diff 5f2b290 HEAD -- docs/sprints/2-in-progress/sprint-14*.md` is empty, so the requirements are byte-identical to round 1's.

Both findings closed, and closed the way the criterion demanded: by running, not by re-reasoning.

================================================================
FINDING 1 — CLOSED. THE RUN HAPPENED AND IT SETTLED FINDING 2 AS A SIDE EFFECT.
================================================================

The criterion was "confirm a headless Master Controller can actually create a sprint under the scoped profile — if that was reasoned rather than run, it is not met." It was run: a real headless Master Controller session via `run-role.js --headless --agent master-controller`, real cost incurred, on a fresh scratch install, executing /sprint-new. It used the Write tool itself, unprompted, and created the sprint.

That is the criterion satisfied, and it is also the disproof of the premise the change was originally built on — which is exactly why the criterion demanded a run. One run answered both findings, which is what "single root cause" should mean.

TWO THINGS DONE BEYOND WHAT I ASKED FOR, both of which close gaps I would otherwise have carried:
  - The same run also executed the printf fallback and diffed it against the Write-tool output:
    byte-identical. That verifies the fallback is genuinely equivalent rather than merely available,
    which nobody asked for and which is the claim that would otherwise sit unchecked.
  - A second run tested the heredoc directly under Master Controller's OWN profile rather than
    carrying the result over from qa1/liveqa's context. Identical rejection ("Contains shell syntax
    (file_redirect) that cannot be statically analyzed"). Assuming that carried over would have been
    reasonable and would also have been the same class of mistake this round exists to fix.

================================================================
FINDING 2 — CLOSED, AND THE CORRECTION IS THE BEST OF ITS KIND THIS PROJECT HAS PRODUCED
================================================================

The note now states what is true, and I verified each checkable claim rather than reading it approvingly:
  - "does NOT disable Write for Master Controller — only qa1 and liveqa lose it": confirmed against
    the shipped HEADLESS_PERMISSION_PROFILES. master-controller disallowedTools: []. It also points
    at the file, so the next reader can check it in one command instead of trusting the sentence.
  - "confirmed by actually running": corroborated by the commit body, which records both runs.
  - The re-diagnosis of what the ORIGINAL defect actually was is the part that matters most and it is
    correct: the old instruction wrote to an absolute /tmp path, which fails twice over — acceptEdits'
    auto-approval is confined to the launch working directory (sprint 12's own confirmed finding), and
    /tmp does not exist on a default Windows box. The relative path already fixes both. So the real
    defect was real; only its explanation was wrong.
  - The printf fallback is kept and correctly reframed as insurance against a stricter profile than
    this framework's default, rather than a workaround for a missing tool.

And it says plainly that the round-1 version claimed the opposite, was wrong, and was caught by QA1 rather than by running it first. Naming your own retracted claim in the artifact is what stops someone rediscovering it from an old transcript, and it is the third time this team has done that rather than quietly swapping the text.

================================================================
FINDING 3 — FOR MASTER CONTROLLER, NOT BLOCKING, AND IT MUST BE FIXED BEFORE THIS SPRINT CLOSES
================================================================

Dev Team flagged this correctly and correctly did not touch it. The sprint file itself, line 38, still says:

  "It instructs writing the temp file *with the Write tool* — which sprint 12's scoped headless
   profile hard-disables, so a headless Master Controller cannot create a sprint at all."

That is the same false premise, in the artifact it originated in. This sprint's own round-2 run disproves it: Master Controller has Write, used it unprompted, and created a sprint.

Why it is not blocking: my verdict is on the build, the build is right, and Dev Team cannot edit a sprint file — making this a CONDITIONAL would create a precondition the role that hits it cannot clear, which this framework has a rule against and which I have argued against four times in the last three sprints.

Why it must still be fixed: the sprint file is the durable record. Right now it will retire into 3-done asserting something this very sprint proved false, and the requirement's own rationale ("fix both together or the file is still broken headless") would read to a future reader as describing a defect that never existed for this role. The change that shipped is still correct — the absolute-path defect was real — so the fix is to correct the stated cause, not the requirement.

Note the sequencing this creates, since it has bitten twice: amending the sprint file after this PASS will change qa1_audit_file_hash and /sprint-dev-done will refuse, requiring a round 3. That round would be a one-line read. Better that than closing on a record that contradicts its own evidence, but decide it deliberately rather than discovering it at dev-done.

================================================================
EVERYTHING ELSE — VERIFIED, UNCHANGED
================================================================

Round-2 diff is one line in .claude/commands/sprint-new.md plus the state file. Nothing else moved.

Re-ran everything rather than carrying round 1's results: ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED; ALL LAUNCHER TESTS PASSED, 125 OK; ALL WORKTREE TESTS PASSED; verify-tarball.sh TARBALL VERIFICATION PASSED, "Installed 0.1.15 (first install)"; package.json 0.1.15.

The one `/tmp` hit remaining across all twelve command files is in sprint-new.md's corrected note, quoting the old absolute path while explaining why it was wrong. Checked the live instruction lines separately: step 2 says `sprint-title.txt`, "a path inside your working directory, never `/tmp`". Prose, not a live path. Req 1's grep-all-twelve criterion holds.

Not re-derived, verified in round 1 and unchanged: Req 2's ASCII proof (zero non-ASCII in non-comment code, zero in 4,660 characters of real captured stdout across a clean run and a conflict run), Req 3's Windows runs and the py-branch-unreachable observation, Req 4 read cold against sprint 10's actual header, Req 5's invariant matching the code including what it does not cover.

RECOMMENDATION

Ship it, once Master Controller decides on Finding 3. /sprint-dev-done 14, then Pipeman ships and publishes 0.1.15, then `verify-publish 14` rather than asserting gitHead by hand.

If line 38 is corrected first, expect the sprint-file hash to change and dev-done to refuse — that is the gate working, and round 3 would be me re-reading one line.

Worth recording once, because the pattern is now four sprints old and this round is the first time it broke cleanly: sprint 12's heredoc, sprint 12's /tmp destination, sprint 13's "docs/sprints never ships," and sprint 14's "Master Controller never has Write" were all claims that a run would have settled and reasoning did not. This round, the run happened first and the claim came second. That is the order that works.

PASS: PASS — round 3. Audited aef6db9, main checkout. Short round by design, as promised: one sub-bullet in the sprint file moved, nothing else.

WHAT MOVED, AND NOTHING ELSE DID

aef6db9 is one file, two insertions, one deletion — byte-for-byte the change I reviewed in the working tree before it was committed, re-confirmed against the committed object rather than assumed. The sprint file's working tree is now clean.

`git diff 813316b HEAD -- scripts/ .claude/ package.json templates/` is EMPTY. The build is byte-identical to what round 2 passed, so round 2's suite results stand on the same bytes and there is nothing to re-run for a documentation-only change. Everything verified in rounds 1 and 2 — Req 1's /tmp sweep across all twelve command files, Req 2's ASCII proof (zero non-ASCII in non-comment code, zero across 4,660 characters of real captured stdout including a conflict run), Req 3's real Windows runs and the py-branch-unreachable observation, Req 4 read cold against sprint 10's actual header, Req 5's invariant, 0.1.15, 125 launcher tests plus smoke, worktree and tarball — stands unchanged and is not re-derived here.

THE CORRECTION — VERIFIED, NOT READ APPROVINGLY

Re-confirmed all three factual claims against the committed file and the live code:
  - "Write was never disabled for Master Controller's profile": master-controller disallowedTools: [].
    Only qa1 and liveqa lose it. Checked against the shipped HEADLESS_PERMISSION_PROFILES, again.
  - "The real defect is /tmp/sprint-title.txt being absolute — outside acceptEdits' working-directory
    confinement, and /tmp does not exist on Windows": both established by running, in sprint 12's
    findings and sprint 14's own VM work respectively.
  - "sprint 11's Req 7 mandated a Write-tool pattern which sprint 12's profile made impossible FOR THE
    TWO ROLES REQ 7 WAS WRITTEN FOR — qa1 and liveqa": accurate. Req 7 was scoped to those two agent
    files, and that scoping is precisely what was lost.

The "where the wrong cause came from" note is the part worth having kept. "Right effect, wrong mechanism" is the correct diagnosis: a real finding, correctly scoped to two roles, generalised to a third with a different profile without checking. A future reader now gets the reasoning error rather than only the corrected conclusion, which is the difference between a fix and a lesson. Fourth time this team has named its own retracted claim in the artifact rather than quietly swapping the text.

Finding 3 from round 2 is closed. The sprint file will now retire into 3-done stating what its own evidence established rather than contradicting it.

ONE THING WORTH RECORDING, BECAUSE IT IS SPRINT 13 EARNING ITS KEEP ON THE VERY NEXT SPRINT

This round exists because /sprint-dev-done refused after the sprint file changed — the qa1_audit_file_hash gate, working exactly as designed. Note which gate did NOT fire: sprint 13's ship-hash exclusion means a docs/sprints/*/*.md change no longer disturbs qa1_audited_tree_hash at all, so the ship gate was never in question here. Before sprint 13 this same correction would have tripped both gates and read as source drift.

That is the overlap sprint 13 removed, behaving correctly on the first sprint after it: one gate catches a sprint-file amendment, the other ignores it, and the round-3 cost is one line rather than a re-audit of the whole build. Recording it because a mechanism working quietly is otherwise invisible, and this one cost four rounds of argument to get right.

RECOMMENDATION

Ship it. /sprint-dev-done 14 will now run clean the first time — the file hash matches the committed file, and the tree hash was never affected. Then Pipeman ships and publishes 0.1.15, then `verify-publish 14` rather than asserting gitHead by hand.

Carried, not blocking, unchanged: the --agents argv budget against Windows' 32,767-char limit; the interactive auth-check ordering from sprint 11 round 1; and the baseline-fixture drift, now scheduled as sprint 16 after four occurrences.
